New director of operations to blend internal focus with community engagement across Sioux Metro area

Submitted
17 hours ago
  • Share
  • Tweet
  • LinkedIn

Sept. 24, 2026

This piece is sponsored by Sioux Metro Growth Alliance.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:39
Instaread

From enhanced events to increased communication, the newest member of the Sioux Metro Growth Alliance leadership team is jumping right into her new role with the regional economic development organization.

As director of operations, Hayley Johnson’s role focuses both internally on SMGA’s day-to-day needs as well as outwardly on its community-focused work.

She oversees organizational operations in addition to assisting with communications and public engagement, along with planning and executing SMGA events.

“A big part of the role will also be working with our communities and partners to make sure we’re communicating effectively, staying connected and delivering on the opportunities we create,” she said.

“Ultimately, I’ll be focused on making sure the organization runs well and that we’re creating meaningful value for the communities we serve.”

Johnson comes to her role from U.S. Rep. Dusty Johnson’s office, where she served in a variety of leadership positions. Her background includes economics, political science, finance and communications.

“In her first weeks on our team, Hayley already has made an impact on our organization and the communities we serve,” said Tyler Tordsen, president and CEO of Sioux Metro Growth Alliance.

“She brings the skills to succeed in this role and definitely will take us to a new level of efficiency and engagement.”

We sat down with Johnson to learn more about her new role and what it will bring to the growing metro area.

What most appeals to you about joining SMGA?

What appeals most to me about joining SMGA is the opportunity to do work that has a real, visible impact on the communities we partner with. I’ve always loved building relationships, bringing people together and finding ways to help move things forward, so economic development feels like a natural fit for me. I’m also excited by the idea of working alongside local leaders, businesses and community partners to help create opportunities and make the Sioux Metro an even better place to live, work and grow. I grew up in a small town in South Dakota, so I appreciate SMGA’s heart for seeing small communities thrive.

What has stood out to you most in your first days on the job as you’ve gotten to know the organization better?

Sioux Metro Growth Alliance is always looking to do more. This is a group that is not content with the status quo. For example, in my first week, I got to jump in to helping with the first-ever Leadership Sioux Metro event. Not only does this organization care deeply about the communities they serve, but they want to be a multiplier when it comes to developing leaders in their member communities.

What are some of your first priorities in taking on your new role?

My first priorities are strengthening organizational operations, increasing public engagement and assisting in executing meaningful events. I want to make sure we have the right systems and processes in place to support SMGA’s work while also finding new ways to tell our story and connect with people across the region. I’m also looking forward to planning and executing events that bring people together and create opportunities for connection and collaboration.

What are some opportunities you’re especially excited to tackle at SMGA?

With the growth and momentum the Sioux Metro has right now, there are a lot of things to be excited about. I’m especially excited about the opportunity to strengthen engagement across the communities SMGA serves while continuing to build meaningful programming and events that bring people together. I also see a lot of opportunity to tell the story of the great things happening across the region and elevate businesses and communities that are driving that growth. Most of all, I’m excited to help SMGA grow its impact and become an even stronger resource for the region.

What do you enjoy doing outside of work?

Outside of work, I stay busy with a mix of fitness, volunteering and quality time with family and friends. I love going on walks with my husband, Jeremiah, working out, grabbing coffee with friends and teaching BodyPump classes at GreatLIFE two nights each week. During the school year, I also spend Wednesday nights at Central Church co-leading an amazing group of 11th grade girls.

When it’s time to relax, I’m usually watching a documentary. True crime and war documentaries have always been favorites, but lately I’ve been fascinated by presidential documentaries. If you’re looking for something new to watch, I have plenty of recommendations!
